q: 1. A volatile substance added to a paint to make its application easy and smooth, is known as
explain: A solvent (thinner) is a volatile liquid that reduces paint viscosity for smoother application, evaporating afterward.

q: 2. Pigments are available in the form of
explain: Pigments are typically supplied as fine powders, later mixed with a vehicle to form paint.

q: 3. PVC stands for .....
explain: PVC is polyvinyl chloride. Option b is the closest to this in the book, and the key gives b.

q: 4. The material generally not used as extender in paints is .....
explain: Silica, gypsum and talc are extenders (inert fillers). Zinc white is a pigment (base), not an extender.

q: 5. Oil varnish generally consists of .....
explain: Oil varnish is made by dissolving resin in linseed oil and turpentine.

q: 6. Snowcrete is one of the patent forms of .....
explain: Snowcrete (like Snowcem) is a patented water-proof cement paint.

q: 7. To give a brilliant finish the type of varnish used, is .....
explain: Spirit varnish dries quickly and gives a brilliant, glossy finish.

q: 8. The defect in painting caused by excessive moisture vaporizing in back to the film is known as
explain: Blistering occurs when trapped moisture vaporizes and pushes up the paint film from beneath, forming bubbles.

q: 9. An extender is used in paints for easy spreading. Which of the following can be used as extender in paints?
explain: Gypsum is commonly used as an extender in paint to improve spreading and reduce cost, without materially affecting color.

q: 10. On which type of surface, lacquer paints are applied?
explain: Lacquer paints, which dry very quickly to a hard glossy finish, are commonly applied on structural steel surfaces.

q: 11. Out of the following, the material which dries quickly is
explain: Polish, being a spirit-based preparation, dries much faster than oil paints, enamel, or varnish.

q: 12. A hydro-carbon material that completely soluble in carbon disulphide is known as
explain: Bitumen is a hydrocarbon material that is completely soluble in carbon disulphide, a key test for its purity/identification.

q: 13. The pigment in paints is mixed to give desired .....
explain: Pigment is added to give the desired colour.

q: 14. The liquid part of the paint is called .....
explain: The liquid part (usually oil) that carries the pigment is the vehicle.

q: 15. The standard width of asbestos cement sheet is
explain: Standard asbestos cement corrugated sheets are commonly manufactured with a width of about 1.23 m.

q: 16. A hydro-carbon material of either natural or pyrogenous origin, and completely soluble in carbon disulphide is known as
explain: Bitumen, whether of natural or refinery (pyrogenous) origin, is defined by its complete solubility in carbon disulphide.

q: 17. The commonly base used in a paint is .....
explain: Any of these can be used as a paint base.

q: 18. Linseed oil is rapidly soluble in .....
explain: As per the answer key, all of these. Linseed oil is soluble in turpentine and naphtha, and the key accepts alcohol too.

q: 19. Cutbacks are used
explain: Cutback bitumen is thinned with a volatile solvent so it can be applied without needing to be heated.

q: 20. The co-efficient of expansion of glass is
explain: Ordinary glass has a relatively high coefficient of thermal expansion, which is why it can crack under sudden temperature changes.

q: 21. In paints, pigment is responsible for:
explain: Pigment is the solid coloring component in paint responsible for its color and opacity.

q: 22. The paints with white lead base are suitable for painting of
explain: White lead base is excellent for wood because it is very durable and flexible, but it is rarely used on iron as it can promote corrosion compared to red lead.

q: 23. The oily liquid in which base and pigment are dissolved to form a paint is called
explain: The vehicle (or binder) is the liquid that holds the pigment and base in suspension and helps it adhere to the surface.

q: 24. The small areas on painted surface enclosed by hair line cracks are called
explain: Crazing refers to the formation of fine, shallow hairline cracks on the surface of the paint.

q: 25. The paint used for automobiles is
explain: Modern automobile finishes often use advanced oil-based paints for a smooth, durable finish.

q: 26. Duco is the trade name for
explain: Duco is a well-known brand of cellulose-based paint commonly used in the automotive industry.

q: 27. French polish is made by dissolving the resin
explain: French polish is a type of spirit varnish made by dissolving shellac in methylated spirit.

q: 28. The pigment used in paints for corrosive resistance is
explain: Red lead (lead tetroxide) is highly effective at preventing the corrosion of iron and steel.

q: 29. The following element of a paint is used as base, pigment as well as drier
explain: Red lead is unique because it serves as a base, provides color (pigment), and acts as an oxidizing drier.

q: 30. Inert filler / adulterant is used in paint to
explain: Inert fillers (extenders) are used to bulk up the paint and make it more economical.

q: 31. Bitumen paint renders
explain: Bituminous paints are primarily used for their excellent protective and anti-corrosive qualities on ironwork.

q: 32. Bitumen is
options: semi solid state is called mineral tar
explain: In civil engineering and materials science, bitumen refers to a highly viscous, sticky black substance that changes form depending on its state and composition. It can be classified by its physical state:Solid state: AsphaltSemi-solid state: Mineral tarFluid state: Petroleum.

q: 33. Mastic asphalt is generally used for
explain: Due to its impermeable nature, mastic asphalt is a standard material for Damp Proof Courses (DPC) and waterproof layer  in buildings.

q: 34. Bitumen may be dissolved in
explain: Bitumen is chemically defined by its solubility in carbon disulphide ($CS_2$).

q: 35. The filler used in plastic bitumen is
explain: Asbestos powder is commonly used as a filler in plastic bitumen to provide fiber reinforcement and stability.

q: 36. The natural rubber is obtained from the...........of the plant.
explain: Natural rubber is processed from latex, a milky sap produced by various plants, most notably the Hevea brasiliensis tree.

q: 37. A good quality bitumen suitable for paving jobs should not indicated a loss in weight more than
explain: When heated, high-quality bitumen should be stable with minimal loss of volatile components (typically <1%).
